lens: Simplicity and elegance: how few primitives and rules, how little bookkeeping, and whether history is a real resource rather than a log bolted on.

scores.design: Riders: tree calculus that reads without consuming
scores.reasons: This is the only design that actually shrinks the calculus. Agent kinds drop from 13 to 6 (leaf, stem, fork, frame, rider, ⊥). The core rules are T1-T9, pass, three copy-out rules and forget. It also removes Dn, Eps, Pair/Unp, P, Nrm, Sup and Seam, plus all the collection special cases. Its history is the most honest of the five. A finished frame is itself the stem or fork it computed, and a K receipt is the frame stepping aside, so programs read history as data rather than as a side log. Labels in place of movement agents and jets, with no spell-out rules, follow from code never being consumed. Four things keep it from a higher score. (1) Thread marks are one per step (359 for add 1 1), which is a per-step log, just stored locally on strands. Exact reversal depends on them, so a bolted-on trace comes back in through the side door. (2) The rules carry hidden bookkeeping: per-rider pass counts, the 'direct holds' special case that conjures a rider plus ⊥, frames with six states, and rider trees that must 'reorganise' when one holder takes a value apart. That last rule is not specified at all. (3) The reversible add is a native 'frame in mode add' routine, not something the rules derive. (4) The port-level rules touch 3-5 agents and have never been run, so the small count is argued, not shown.

scores.design: Tree gas: disp's tree-calculus net run as a reversible lattice gas
scores.reasons: It has one clean organising principle: every move is an involution on a 2x2x2 block, paid for by a per-site demon. That single principle replaces four substrate mechanisms (records, bonds, gathering, cascading forget). The Φn fan, where eraser, normalizer and duplicator become one agent with a count of 0, 1 or 2, turns 14 rules into one written scheme ('make n nodes of X's kind, put Φn on each child'). That is the best small unification on the table. Bennett's cleanup comes for free by counting the clock back. But the calculus is untouched: 26 rules plus 3 collections, and the design says so itself. It adds three slot kinds where one would do (blank, fuel, and ash tagged with one of 9 kinds), plus canonical seating, an arm reorder for Sel, unfold moves and a fan-output swap. History is mostly passive heat in the bath. The only time-travel is all-or-nothing reversal of a closed lattice, which is a global property, not a local resource. The one usable history (fans left by graft) disappears as soon as anything reads the sum. Laziness (wanted bits, pulses) is admitted to be non-bijective and is still unsolved, which is the largest piece of bookkeeping left over.

scores.design: Footprint nets: every rewrite leaves a footprint wired to what it made
scores.reasons: The core idea is elegant and stated in one line: the used-up pair is the receipt, and undoing is a two-agent meeting on a back wire. The meet/part and emit/absorb law pairs are uniform and apply to every rule. Holding the arms directly in T and Q removes Pair/Unp and P, a real simplification. The 26 rules read as 'carrier x matter' plus collector rules. History is fully usable: undo anywhere, causally, in parallel, and garbage collection by running back. But the bookkeeping is heavy. Every agent gains a back port. A footprint's kind encodes the rule plus a bitmask of which products are out (5+4 bits), with up to 10 wire ends. Q has 6 ports. History is one footprint per rewrite (8.7-37x the program), so it is a complete event log made of matter: local, but still a log, not something the program chose to keep. Code that should leave no history needs a second, unrelated mechanism (exchange walkers with trail ports). Bennett's cleanup is impossible inside the net. So there are two history mechanisms and a large state per footprint.

scores.design: Three moves, no records: the tree-calculus net with its losses priced, reversed by running inverse programs
scores.reasons: It is the smallest change to the core: one copy bit on L/S/F, one portless heat particle H, and an absorbing edge, with fuel as plain empty seats (no fuel particle). Its best property is clean and checkable: every rule read backward is a valid tree-calculus equation, so a backward fluctuation can never change the answer. But it simplifies by moving the hard part off the core. History is not a core resource at all. Two-way programs are pairs of trees (f, f†) with a hand-written inverse. Nothing derives sub_keep from add_keep, and a hand-written inverse silently dropped data once. Reversal of ordinary code still needs rev.rs or tc. The copy bit is an admittedly inaccurate heat ledger: it undercounts when both copies die and overcounts otherwise. The two-way binary adder written this way costs 2.2-6x the events and erases 529 code nodes per call, so the cost lands in program bulk instead. The rule table is the same 29 lines with bit-conditional variants of Eps.

scores.design: Loan net: room is borrowed, heat is spent
scores.reasons: It reads best as slogans: room is borrowed, heat is spent, a waiting duplicator is a loan, a pending operation is its own undo, reading spends it. It mostly deletes things: P rules, Seam, global temperature, cooling, dnroom and the substrate. One mechanism (per-site demons) replaces four. But the elegance is partly bought by giving things up. History is only 'what has not happened yet', so it cannot rewind ordinary programs, and criterion 7 is met only for add before the sum is read. Its reversible primitives (Ap, Un) are a special-purpose unary-add/append pair, not a general principle. The design concedes that binary add would need about six more agent kinds and sixteen rules. Keeping block maps one-to-one relies on a hack: rules with the same right-side shape put different numbers of quanta into the demon (1/2/3 for L/S/F, and 4 vs 7, 21 vs 24). The pinned/closing drive split is extra per-rule bookkeeping. Heat is about one quantum per step, 'the drive dominates', so the accounting is mostly noise relative to what was actually forgotten.

best_ideas_to_graft: Riders: reading never consumes code. Code is persistent matter and a frame reads it through a pointer, which removes fix's per-call code copies (87-95% of duplicator work). Movement agents and jets then become one-node labels with no spell-out rules.
Riders: values are made of history. A finished application frame IS the stem or fork it built, and a K drop leaves the frame itself as the receipt, so the history is the data rather than a side log.
Tree gas: one fan agent Φn (n = 0 erase, 1 observe, 2 copy) gives one written rule scheme 'Φn·X makes n nodes of X's kind and puts Φn on each child', in place of three agent families.

Tree gas: every move is written together with its inverse and paid by a per-site Creutz demon. One principle then replaces records, bonds, gathering and Metropolis acceptance, and Bennett's cleanup is 'copy the answer to a shadow register, then count the clock back'.

Three moves: the checkable invariant that every rule read right-to-left is a valid tree-calculus equation, so backward fluctuations cannot change the answer. Worth adding to validate() for whatever core wins.
Three moves / Loan net: fuel is just an empty seat. Drop Tree gas's separate fuel particle, so the only new slot content is heat.
Footprint nets: T and Q hold triage arms directly, removing Pair/Unp and their fusion rule.
Footprint nets: any undo that must happen should be a two-agent meeting along a wire (back port), never a k-body gathering. This is the stated cause of the substrate's 10-12x slower way back.

Loan net: frame un-copy as 'repaying a loan' (an eraser reaching an unbuilt copy), and treat a pending operation as its own undo record that reading spends. A clean vocabulary for what is free and what costs heat.

Tree gas / Riders: Cuccaro-style binary add with carries parked either in the data (a's bits) or in a walker's local thread and consumed on the way back. This is the model of history a program uses up, which every winner should support without a native special case.

lens: Locality and parallelism on the strand lattice: does every step stay inside a 2x2x2 block with no ids, tables or far reads, and how do rounds, width and clocks compare with the measured designs (lazy net 631 rounds / width 12 for add 2 3; walkers 9.4-51x the rounds; substrate going back at 10-12x its forward clocks; README: one move per block costs 5-7x the clocks of random turns, a turn for every site 2-2.5x)?

scores.design: Three moves, no records (tree-calculus net with losses priced, reversed by inverse programs)
scores.reasons: Most of its locality and parallelism claims are measured on the real lattice, not estimated. Every line is today's two-agent rewrite (three agents for the unpaired-eraser line) plus seats and H in one block. The copy bit is a per-node field and H drifts like idle matter: no ids, no bond_de position lookups, no gather. Forward width is the lazy net's unchanged (add 2 3: 631 rounds, width 12). Going back means running the inverse program forward, so the way back has the same width. It is measured on the latest lattice: sub_keep takes 1.53x add_keep's clocks and rsub 1.06x radd's, against the substrate's 9.8-12x. Hard knocks: (1) Reversible code pays in depth. radd takes 2,797 rounds at 4 bits against relay's 556, five times deeper, and 48k clocks against 7.3k. So a program that wants to be reversible gives up most of the parallelism a lookahead or relay adder has. (2) With no records, any stem can fluctuate back into an apply on a leaf. That backward branching is untested at the current drive, and a deterministic synchronous schedule that settles overlapping rewrites reversibly is admitted to be open. (3) H holds a seat until it reaches the edge, so erasure is capped by surface area; crowding could cut width in the middle of wide runs.

scores.design: Loan net (room is borrowed, heat is spent)
scores.reasons: It is the most local design, because it adds almost nothing: rules 1-23 are rules.rs minus the suspension rules. The contacts (repay, dead work, unpaired, un-append) are the lattice's existing collection moves, which touch a waiting agent's port in the same site or the next. Demons are per site, heat moves one quantum to a neighbour, and only edge sites drain. Width and depth are the net's (631/12, 1,324/36, 685/144), and nothing joins the critical path. The reversible primitives are chains whose inverse involves two agents already joined by a wire, the cheap case for meeting. Append runs in parallel across independent data. Hard knocks: (1) It is local largely because it drops whole-run reversal, so its claim that going back stays local is never tested. (2) The demon-full gate plus O(L^2) edge drain means a wide fork (relay 16-bit, about 150 rewrites a round) heats its middle and throttles itself. The design admits this and does not avoid it; the gate is a global cap on width enforced locally. (3) Swapping global temperature for local demons changes movement dynamics the lattice was tuned on, untested. (4) Its unary add is about 2a+2 rounds of a sequential chain, fine, but there is no binary reversible add, so no parallel reversible arithmetic.

scores.design: Footprint nets (every rewrite leaves a footprint wired to what it made)
scores.reasons: It has the best idea for parallel undo. Each undo is a two-agent meeting along a back wire (absorb one unused product, then split once nothing is out). That directly targets README line 1529: the substrate's 10-12x way back is nearly all an undo waiting for its products to come back together in one block. The abstract measurements are good: forward 0.94-1.08x the current table's rounds, backward 0.55-1.09x forward, widest backward round 171-3,058. No ids: the key is a wire. Hard knocks on the lattice: (1) Port and switchboard budget. Every agent gains a back port, Q has 6, and a footprint has up to 6 wire ends, or 10 while partly taken back. That exceeds the 3-port cell and pressures the 8-pairing switchboard, which the README measured as the main crowding cost (6 pairings already costs about 40% more clocks than 8). (2) History is physical matter: 8.7-37x the program, a peak of 6.2-8.1x the live agents. Back strands use link capacity (4 strands per link, and 3 measured as much slower) and tie footprints to products that move, which brings the bond and drag problem back in another form. (3) Its own first experiment keeps a position-read anchor, so the decisive test is not yet local. (4) Demand is an outside controller that only runs forward. Exchange code that leaves no history is one sequential walker (2n+1 steps). (5) The prototype's scheduler differs from rev.rs's (873 against 631 rounds), so only ratios hold.

scores.design: Tree gas (reversible lattice gas with Creutz demons, fan particle, ash)
scores.reasons: Locally it is clean. Each move reads and writes one 2x2x2 block plus that block's demons, the dice are a hash of block and clock, and canonical seating is local. Ash and fuel hop between neighbours. The collection contacts are today's. Width is the net's. Hard knocks on parallelism: (1) Exact reversal by counting the clock back needs each clock's update to be an involution. Today's chip schedule (a turn for every site, later turns dropped if they see a site an earlier turn changed) is a sequence of overlapping moves with a drop rule that depends on history, so it is not an involution. That pushes the design to one move per block, or moves on disjoint sites, and the README measured one move per block at 5-7x the clocks of random turns against 2-2.5x. The claimed 1.0-1.5x the plain lattice's clocks is therefore probably optimistic by about 2-3x. (2) Reversal is global and all-or-nothing: the whole closed lattice runs back, so one region cannot run back while another runs forward, and Bennett's cleanup doubles total clocks. (3) 160-1,675 ash particles hold slots while they diffuse about L^2 clocks to the boundary, which crowds busy regions. (4) Demand pulses recast as energy may random-walk instead of moving one strand per clock, and laziness is worth 40-66%. (5) Moves spanning two blocks wait for a suitable offset, the same block-edge loss the README already pays.

scores.design: Riders (tree calculus that reads without consuming)
scores.reasons: Its abstract numbers are strong (0.17-0.19x the work, 0.52-0.59x the depth of the lazy net), but the model has no space, and the design's spatial story breaks this lens. (1) Code stands still and every application of a function happens at its one copy, so frames converge on hot code. That makes a spatial sequencing point, and site capacity (K slots) and 8-pairing switchboards serialize it. 'Riders pile up like bosons' has no counterpart on a lattice with bounded slots. (2) Rules are not really block-local. T4 and T7 re-insert a frame onto a different wire ('A is inserted on y's wire just above R_f'), T9 lays a new wire, and when code and argument are apart the frame's halves talk by pulses along the wire between them, so latency grows with distance. READDIST measured reads at 9-64 sites from the loaded code, against copies 1-4 strands from their reader. (3) A step touches 3-5 agents, harder to seat in one block than a two-agent rewrite. (4) Sharing trees of riders cost passes (+3-15%) and need reorganizing when one holder takes a value apart. (5) Width drops to 6-78 against the net's 12-152, and the relay adders are 1.31-1.46x deeper than with movement agents. (6) Thread marks (one per step, 359 for add 1 1) lengthen wires without bound. The bud move fixes hot spots only by bringing copying back.

best_ideas_to_graft: From Footprint nets: make every undo a two-agent meeting along a wire (absorb one unused product at a time, split once nothing is out), never a k-body gathering. Its first experiment is the cheapest decisive test of what causes the substrate's 10-12x way back: products drifting off, or many agents having to meet at once. Run it whichever design wins.

From Three moves: going back means running the inverse program forward on the same net, so the way back has the net's width. It is already measured on the lattice at 1.06-1.53x forward clocks. Also take the 1-bit copy mark on L/S/F as a purely local stand-in for 'is this a copy' when pricing erasure.

From Loan net: split the drive per rule into pinned (the reverse can start only where this step ended, so a small drive will do) and closing (the reverse could start at many places in the block, so it needs about kT ln of that count). Also take the demon-full gate as a local brake on runaway width, and loading every application as a waiting apply so the suspension (P) rules go.

From Tree gas: per-site Creutz demons in place of a global temperature and cooling phase. Pair every move kind with its inverse (add unfold, BFACF kink insertion, as fold's inverse). Merge eraser, normalizer and duplicator into one fan particle with a count of 0, 1 or 2. Caution: exact reversal by counting the clock back needs a clock schedule that is an involution, so the schedule's cost must be measured against the README's 5-7x (one move per block) against 2-2.5x (a turn for every site).

From Riders: treat movement shapes and jets as labels on persistent code nodes with no spell-outs. Keep 'bud' (a refundable copy of a code node's top layer, merged back when unread) as the spatial move the energy chooses, as an option on top of the lazy duplicator, not as a replacement for it.

lens: Physical realisability on a reversible or quantum block-update substrate. Are the local updates actually bijections? Are conservation laws real and checkable per block? Are copy and delete priced honestly, with no hidden global state, unbounded counters, or heat that goes uncounted?

scores.design: Tree gas (reversible lattice gas, fuel in, ash out, the bath holds the history)
scores.reasons:
This is the only design that builds bijectivity in by construction instead of claiming it. Every move is an involution on one 2x2x2 block. The pairing is chosen by dice = hash(block, clock), which depends only on position and clock, not on what the block holds. So overlapping candidate rewrites in one block resolve the same way going forward and going back, which settles the deterministic-schedule question Three moves leaves open. Each clock is a product of involutions on disjoint blocks, so counting the clock down inverts the run exactly. That is sound Margolus/Toffoli partitioning. Slots (agents + fuel + ash + blanks) and energy (one unit per non-blank slot, plus demons) are both conserved and can be checked per block. The Creutz demon replaces Metropolis acceptance with an invertible map on (block, demon). Ash is a real particle that takes a seat and leaves through the edge, so the surface-area limit on erasure falls out naturally, and the step-0 static check of right-side uniqueness is the right test.

The deductions are real. (1) Demand (wanted bits and pulses) is not bijective today, and recasting it as demon energy is untested. Laziness is the part of the machine that matters most for speed, so a non-bijective controller sits at the heart of a supposedly reversible substrate. (2) Collection by contact (un-copy, dead, unpaired) runs backward from configurations that occur all the time: any wire plus two fuel can sprout a duplicator and an eraser, and two erasers plus an ash A can re-form an apply. That rests on canonical seating plus confluence. The design admits this leaks heat when a duplicator copies before the eraser arrives, and the leak is unbounded at temperature. (3) Ash tagged with 9 kinds is information-bearing, not thermalised, heat. Calling it heat before it mixes is fine, but the claim of kT ln 3 per erase undercounts drive dissipation, which (as Loan net points out) dominates. (4) Exact reversal needs a closed lattice, and a closed lattice heats up without bound because demons are 4-6 bits. (5) The Bennett shadow register XORs a site's agent fields, but the answer's wiring spans switchboards and strands. Whether the shadow captures wire topology is not specified.

scores.design: Footprint nets (every rewrite leaves a footprint wired to what it made)
scores.reasons:
Meet/part and emit/absorb are honest bijections. The footprint's kind encodes the rule plus a mask of which products are out, so the inverse is unique without ids. Absorb is a two-agent step over a real back wire, and that check is local. Because nothing but commit merges two states into one, a small drive really is enough (Bennett's unbranched case). The prototype reversed 21 calls and 8,000 random terms agent for agent, the strongest evidence of injectivity in the set. Making undo a two-body meeting directly attacks the substrate's measured 10-12x slow way back, and the first experiment isolates exactly that variable.

Physically it is expensive and partly incomplete. History grows one footprint per rewrite (8.7-37x the loaded program), so space grows linearly in time, and commit costs about one unit per rewrite, no better than an irreversible machine. Footprints have up to 10 wire ends, beyond the 8-pairing switchboard, and every agent gains a port. Back wires are physical strands that stretch and consume link capacity, and none of that is measured. Demand is an outside controller that runs forward only and is not recorded, so the physical device is not closed. Bennett's cleanup cannot be done inside the net, so the only zero-history code is a sequential walker. Heat particles per commit are fine. The heat floor argument (Boyd-Mandal-Crutchfield) is correct but not achieved locally.

scores.design: Loan net (room is borrowed, heat is spent)
scores.reasons:
Its heat accounting is the most honest in the set. It admits that the drive, not erasure, dominates dissipation (about 2,100 steps against 160 erase rewrites for add 2 3). It sorts rules into pinned and closing, with the drive needed set by backward branching (Bennett's kT ln of the number of predecessors). Room as a conserved per-block reservoir, and copying ahead gated by room and demon temperature, are physical and local.

The central bijectivity claim is broken, though. Rules whose right sides have the same shape (4 and 7; 21 and 24) are told apart only by how many quanta they put into the demon. Demon quanta are indistinguishable and the demon state is a number, so a final state with demon d' has two possible pasts (d'-1 or d'-2 with the same configuration). The block map is not one-to-one, and the design itself says it holds only 'until the heat mixes', which in a 4-bit counter is immediate. Every closing step whose reverse could start anywhere in the block is a logical merge: this is an irreversible Brownian machine with an energy ledger attached, not a reversible substrate. The 4-bit demon saturates, and the gate that makes rewrites wait when it is full is a further non-bijective element. It also gives up rewinding outright. In return it is simple and its numbers can be checked.

scores.design: Riders (tree calculus that reads without consuming)
scores.reasons:
Reading in place without consuming is physically fine in the computational basis (a controlled read), and never copying code removes most fan-out heat. Blanks as fuel conserve particle number per block, and forget is the only irreversible step.

The physics is argued, not built. The bijectivity of the port-level rules (3-5 agents per step) is unchecked; the abstract model checks only answers and counts. The rider's pass count is an unbounded counter inside a supposedly finite-state agent. Thread marks, one per step, pile up on a frame-to-rider wire without bound, but strand capacity is finite, so the mechanism that makes each reverse unique cannot fit a fixed site alphabet. T4 and T7 'step aside' by inserting the frame onto y's wire, which can be beyond the block. Forget's price (about log2 of the places a rider could point) needs global knowledge of the code size and is not a local rule. Matter only grows (1.8-21x with marks), and hot spots at shared code fight the switchboard's capacity. Direction set by 'demand-set bias' inherits the same non-bijective demand problem as the others.

scores.design: Three moves, no records (losses priced, reversed by running inverse programs)
scores.reasons:
Treating H as a seat-occupying particle absorbed at the edge is good physics, and reading every line as a tree-calculus equation means backward fluctuations cannot corrupt the answer.

Under this lens it is the weakest. (1) The rules are not bijections: lines 13 and 14 both produce 'Unp, Eps', line 25's bit-1 case produces vacuum, and nothing tags these right sides. The design admits that backward branching is large and that a deterministic reversible schedule is open. (2) The copy bit is thermodynamically wrong. Erasing a bit-1 node is free even after its twin has been read, taken apart or erased, which is exactly the orphaned-copy case Wolpert-Kolchinsky price. Erasing a bit-0 original while its bit-1 twin lives is overcharged. The design calls its ledger a 'local estimate'. (3) The control information lost at a dispatch is never counted as H. (4) 'Reversal' means running a hand-written inverse program, a programming discipline rather than a physical inverse of the dynamics. One-way code cannot be rewound at all. (5) The quantum reading is asserted, with no unitary story for the colliding right sides.

best_ideas_to_graft: From Tree gas: make every move an involution on one block, with the pairing chosen by hash(block, clock) and paid through a per-site Creutz demon. Counting the clock down then inverts the run exactly, and overlapping redexes in one block resolve deterministically and reversibly.

From Tree gas: run a static check in validate() that every rule's right side, under canonical seating, is unique and conserves slots and energy. This is the cheapest way to catch the right-side collisions that sink Loan net and Three moves.

Resolve colliding right sides with distinguishable particles (ash tagged by kind, or Tree gas's reordered Sel arms), never with differing amounts of indistinguishable demon quanta. Loan net's version is not injective.

From Footprint nets: undo as a two-body meet between a product and its maker over one back wire (emit/absorb), with the footprint's kind = rule + mask of products out. Also its first experiment (a per-product, anchored undo on substrate.rs) as the diagnostic for whether the 10-12x slow way back comes from k-body undo or from products drifting away.

From Loan net: price the drive per rule by backward branching. Pinned rules run on a fraction of a quantum, closing rules need about kT ln of the number of places their reverse could start. The drive, not erasure, is most of the heat bill and should be reported as such.
From Loan net and Tree gas: copy ahead only where the block has spare room and a cool demon, so self-reproduction is limited by local fuel and temperature rather than by a global threshold.

From Tree gas and Three moves: heat as a particle that takes a seat and drifts to the edge, so sustained erasure is limited by the lattice's surface (O(L^2) per clock) automatically, with no global ledger.

From Tree gas: refund a copy only at a fan frontier (un-copy while the duplicator still joins the twins). This is the one place a free delete is thermodynamically justified. Do not use Three moves' per-node copy bit, which misprices orphaned copies.
For all of them: recast demand (wanted bits, pulses) as demon energy spent on pulses, or count its non-bijective changes per run. Until then no design here is a closed reversible system.

lens: Expressiveness for disp: does every compiled tree-calculus program run, and with what overhead; can reversible add and other reversible programs leave no history; is code reused instead of copied.

scores.design: Riders: tree calculus that reads without consuming
scores.reasons: Strongest on reusing code. The matter rule (reading never takes a node apart) and the rider rule (a duplicator that does not copy) remove fix's copy on every call. They also remove the 87-95% of duplicator work that is spent copying code. The model measured 0.17-0.19x the lazy net's work and 0.52-0.59x its depth on all 21 calls in calls.txt, and every answer was correct: the best claimed overhead on this panel for running compiled disp. Because code persists, a label is a fact about one node, so movement agents and jets fire at any depth (inside fib too) with no spell-out rules. That gives disp's .opt.disp overrides a much better home. Bennett's cleanup really works here: copy-out (C1-C3) reads the answer without consuming it, so 'copy the answer, then run back' is possible, which the footprint net admits it cannot do. Against it: compiled disp is not history-free by itself. add 2 3 leaves 154 receipts (51 with labels), plus about one thread mark per step (359 for add 1 1). A run with no history needs a hand-written native 'add mode' frame installed as a label, which is a new primitive per routine, not a property of the calculus. The rules at port level (T4's 'A steps aside', T9's new outer frame) were argued, not run, and nothing checked bijectivity. The model has no space, so the 0.17x work may not become fewer clocks once frames crowd at code that cannot move. Matter only grows: 1.3-9.3x the loaded program, or 1.8-21x counting marks. Unwinding work nobody wants needs demand that can be withdrawn, which the leases experiment already found costly.

scores.design: Tree gas: disp's tree-calculus net run as a reversible lattice gas
scores.reasons: Keeps the 26 rules wire for wire, so every compiled program runs and is checked against the abstract net; the only change is the order of Sel's arms. The fan Φn scheme (n = 0, 1 or 2 copies) folds the eraser, normalizer and duplicator into one family without losing any rule. It also gives the most general reversibility: Bennett's cleanup as physics. Count the clock back after XOR-ing the answer into blank shadow registers, and any disp program yields (x, f x) with no heat in twice the clocks, with no inverse program and no trace. Under this lens that is the biggest win for 'reversible programs leave no history'. Against it: the claim that graft-based add_keep makes 0 ash is overstated. The Three moves design measured an add_keep of the same structure and found 18 loaded-code nodes erased per call, and those are originals, not fan copies, so under this design's own rules they become ash. The same applies to the nested-triage Cuccaro column, because those are real arms of the loaded program that were never taken. Using the fan as history (subtract by un-copying at the n fans) is elegant but fragile: any read of the sum spends it. The 1.0-1.5x overhead is an estimate. Exact reversal depends on making demand bijective, which is untested and worth 40-66% of speed. Code is still copied: fix's copies run on a closed fuel loop and un-copy refunds them, which is cheap copying, not reuse.

scores.design: Three moves, no records
scores.reasons: Has the most concretely demonstrated two-way layer. add_keep, sub_keep, radd and rsub are written in real disp, said to pass probe.sh -r, and were measured on both the abstract net and the lattice. dagger and seq are one-line ordinary disp, so two-way programs compose as a library with no new rules. One technique is worth keeping: read a value away by dispatch instead of dropping it (the `bit` helper, the succ leaf in sub_keep), so no input data is ever erased. Every compiled program runs unchanged on the 29 lines at plain-lattice cost. But one-way code cannot be reversed: that takes rev.rs as a debugger or the eager tc/tck, and there is no Bennett route inside the physics for ordinary programs. Two-way code compiled through bracket abstraction is heavy: radd costs 2.2x ripple_add and 6x relay_add, and it erases 529 loaded-code nodes per call. So 'leaves no history' holds for data but not for code heat. Every inverse is written by hand, and a wrong one can silently drop data (sub_keep's first version did). Code is reused only by lazy copy-and-merge.

scores.design: Footprint nets: every rewrite leaves a footprint wired to what it made
scores.reasons: Reversing arbitrary compiled code is best verified here. All 21 calls plus 8,000 random terms run forward and back to the loaded net agent for agent, at 1.02x the forward rounds and 0.81x for going back. So every disp program runs and can be undone causally in parallel. Uncomputing the branches that missed the answer isolates the exact real loss (24 agents for add 2 3, 83 for fib 3), which is a useful diagnostic. It fails the 'no history' half. Every rewrite leaves a footprint (8.7-37x the loaded program). Bennett's cleanup cannot run inside the net, because reading uses the answer up. Code with no history means an exchange walker, which is sequential and covers only a hand-written binary add, and the native unary carrier G still leaves 2|a|+2 footprints. There is no code reuse: the S rule's duplicator copies code as before (28-34% of footprints). A footprint needs up to 10 ports while partly taken back, which exceeds the switchboard. Absolute rounds come from a simpler scheduler (873 against 631 for add 2 3).

scores.design: Loan net: room is borrowed, heat is spent
scores.reasons: Ordinary compiled programs run, but the design drops suspensions on an untested assumption about demand and gives up rewinding them altogether; it can only undo operations still pending. Reversible add needs the new Ap/Un primitives, swapped in by the loader. Any program that triages that primitive needs hundreds of nodes spelled out, and un-append works only while the sum is unread. There is no binary reversible add: by the design's own account Cuccaro's column would take about six agent kinds and sixteen rules, and it was left out, so the two-way layer reaches far less than the injective functions. Code reuse is only lazy loans that get repaid, which is today's un-copy collection with a price attached. The pinned versus closing classification of steps and 'a pending operation is its own undo' are sound but narrow.

best_ideas_to_graft: From Riders: matter that is never consumed by reading (a rider is a duplicator without the copy). Code stays put and is shared by any number of frames, which removes fix's per-call copies and the 87-95% of copying that is code.
From Riders: labels on persistent code nodes in place of movement agents and jets. A jet then fires at any depth with no spell-out rules, which is a clean home for .opt.disp overrides.

From Tree gas: Bennett as physics. Every block update is its own inverse, so after XOR-ing the answer into shadow registers, counting the clock back gives (x, f x) for any compiled program with no inverse program written.
From Tree gas: the single fan Φn (n = 0, 1, 2) unifying eraser, normalizer and duplicator, read as Bounded Linear Logic's 0, 1, + bounds.
From Three moves: two-way programs as plain-disp pairs (f, f†) with one-line dagger and seq, plus the habit of reading a value away by dispatch instead of dropping it, so input data is never erased.
From Three moves: a copy bit on L/S/F, so local heat accounting can tell refundable copies from originals.
From Riders and Cuccaro: park the carries in the walker's own beads instead of in a's bits, so the kept operand can stay shared while the add leaves nothing behind.

From Footprint nets: the verification harness (thousands of random terms, forward and back, checked agent for agent), and uncomputing the branches that missed the answer to measure each run's exact real loss.
From Loan net: tag each rule pinned or closing (whether its reverse can start only where it ended, or anywhere its shape appears), which tells how much drive each step needs.

lens: Correctness and rigour: are the rules complete and actually bijective where claimed, are the citations used faithfully, are the claimed numbers plausible. I checked the rule tables against evaluators/rust-ca-lattice/crate/src/rules.rs (26 rules), checked each design's room and fuel arithmetic and adder algebra by hand, looked at the scratch prototypes, and re-ran /tmp/fpnet/randtest.py: 4000 of 4000 random terms gave the right answer and ran back exactly to the loaded net.

scores.design: Footprint nets
scores.reasons:
The only design whose bijection claim follows from its construction rather than from an assertion.
- How the bijection works: a footprint's kind is (which rule, which products are out). So meet/part and emit/absorb are each one-to-one. Absorb is a binary meeting along the product's back wire, which needs no global uniqueness argument.
- Prototype: it exists and reproduces. I re-ran randtest.py: 4000 of 4000 terms agree with an independent tree-calculus evaluator and return exactly to the loaded net under random interleavings of forward and backward steps. The 21 compiled calls are also claimed.
- Carry-walker binary adder, checked by hand. The down map (c,a,b) -> (maj, a⊕c, b⊕c) is a bijection on 3 bits. The up step's c_i = c ⊕ (a'∧b') correctly recovers the carry and writes (a, a⊕b⊕c). The overflow claim is right, because (a, a+b mod 2^n) is itself a bijection.
- Native G carrier: the footprint count 2|a|+2 matches the rules (6 for a=2).
- S, K and triage rewired without Pair/Unp: all three match tree calculus.
- The collector table is incomplete. There are no rules for E·E or E·N, justified only by 'never happened in 21 programs'.
- 'Commit costs 1 unit' is a convention, not a Landauer figure; a footprint holds more than 1 bit.
- The Melgratti-style claim that backward never leaves the forward path is plausible but argued, not proved.
- The prototype keys agents by ids, so 'no ids' is shown only abstractly. Lattice back-wire lengths and the port counts (up to 10 wire ends against an 8-pairing switchboard) are honestly flagged as unmeasured or over budget.
- Citations (RCCS, CCSK, Cardelli, Dijkstra-Scholten, Baker) are used faithfully.

scores.name: x
scores.design: Tree gas
scores.reasons:
The most careful bookkeeping of the five. Δf = 2 − (fresh agents) checks out for every rule I tried (A·L +1, T·S −3, T·F −2, Sel·S −3, Sel·F −4, Unp·Pair +2, all the Φ2 and Φ1 rules, and the collections). Ash tagged by kind for both erasure and dead work genuinely makes those rules injective on block plus bath. It also spots and fixes a real clash in rules.rs: T1·L and Sel·L produce identical Unp+Eps right sides, and reordering Sel's arms to ⟨⟨x,b⟩,w⟩ separates them.

Gaps:
- **The demand rules as written are not an involution.** A pulse meeting a set wanted bit gives a unit to the demon, and a pulse meeting an unset bit sets it. Then (bit set, no pulse, demon d+1) is the partner of both (unset, pulse, d+1) and (set, pulse, d).
- **The pairing choice is unspecified.** 'Pairing chosen by hash(block, clock)' must choose the same pairing from P and from Q when a block holds several candidate redexes. This is never specified, and a Margolus clock is an involution only if it is.
- **Frank's conditional reversibility is cited beyond its scope.** It is used to excuse right sides that occur only on reachable states, but a block map must be a permutation on all block states. The design then concedes spurious reverse moves (S+fuel -> A·L) and a heat leak from them.
- **The speed figures are unmeasured.** 'Back = forward clocks' is sound for a closed deterministic reversible CA. The 1.0-1.5x forward estimate is a guess, though it is labelled as one.
- **The graft/ungraft history argument depends on unread fans and need-gated Dn.** It is plausible but not run.
- **The numbers it borrows are consistent with the other designs:** 2,109 rewrites and 160/161 erased with 145 of them copies.

scores.design: Three moves, no records
scores.reasons:
Strong empirical side:
- Real disp programs (add_keep, sub_keep, radd, rsub) were probe-tested.
- The lattice clocks were measured over several seeds.
- An exact classifier separates erased copies from erased originals (427 erased, 399 copies, 28 H).
- The room deltas on all 29 lines check out.
- The sub_keep fix (reading the succ leaf by dispatch instead of dropping it) shows a real audit for silently dropped data.

But the headline claim, 'with its blanks counted, each line maps one local configuration to exactly one other, so it is a bijection', is false on its own table:
- Lines 13 and 14 (T1·L and Sel·L → Unp, Eps) have identical right sides. It keeps rules.rs's arm order, so nothing tells them apart.
- Line 23 sends Eps on the result of A, T1 or Sel to the same Eps, Eps, with no residue. That is a three-to-one merge with no heat charged.
- Lines 25-27 at bit 1 turn agents into blanks or into Eps, Eps. That is many-to-one against the vacuum and against line 29 (Eps·Pair → Eps, Eps).

The design half-admits this later ('backward branching is large'). That turns it into a Brownian, drive-paid picture, not a bijective one.

Other problems:
- The copy-bit heat ledger is thermodynamically unsound: bit-1 erasure is free even when the twin is gone. It is admitted as only an estimate.
- The summary's 'back costs 1.06-1.5x' does not match its own measured 1.53x.
- Reversal is by hand-written inverse programs, which is sound but proves nothing about the core.

scores.design: Riders
scores.reasons:
The headline numbers are not measured on the machine as specified. They come from /tmp/riders/sim.py, which I inspected: a persistent pointer DAG with frames and pointers, no ports, no reverse execution and no bijectivity check (the design admits the port-level rules are 'argued, not yet run').

Unsupported or contradicted claims:
- **Reversibility is assumed.** 'Each rule is a bijection between its two sides' is asserted. The design itself concedes that without the per-step thread marks some states have two pasts. Those marks (359 for add 1 1) are a per-step log, which undercuts 'no record table'.
- **The rider's pass count breaks bounded state.** It is an unbounded integer in one agent, and on hot shared code it grows with the number of readers.
- **T4/T7 'step aside' is underspecified.** It re-splices wires between distant parts of the code: R_f goes from the fork's left child over to its right child, and A is inserted on y's wire.
- **Its work figures are apples to oranges.** 0.17x the work and 0.52x the depth compare frame steps that merge 2-3 net rewrites, and charge nothing for sharing. This is acknowledged, but the comparison still carries the summary.

What holds up:
- The native adders are arithmetically right: unary fuel is 4 blanks = 2 forks + 2 leaves, and in the binary bead adder each pop is justified because maj is recomputable from what is present.
- The citations are mostly faithful (Keller, Abramsky, Cardelli).

scores.design: Loan net
scores.reasons:
The arithmetic is right:
- 20 tree rules = 26 − 6 P rules.
- Every room delta checks out (T·S +3, D·F +4, E·L −2, repay −2, Un −1).
- The unary trace really takes 3a+2 steps and borrows 2a seats.
- Un-append then repay restores (a, b).

But the physical claims contradict themselves:
- **Bijection versus forgetting.** It says 'every step inside the lattice is a permutation of block states (Margolus)', yet also 'each step forgets its own record immediately', and that closing steps' reverses 'could start wherever the shape appears'. Those cannot both hold.
- **The demons cannot hold what is forgotten.** Creutz demons are counters of identical quanta and cannot store which rule fired. So 'the information a run forgets sits in demon quanta' (as D'Souza-Margolus's positioned heat particles do) is not supported.
- **Clashing right sides are left unspecified.** Rules 4/7 and 21/24 are said to be told apart by depositing 'different amounts', with no amounts given. U·Pr and Ap·L also both yield joined wires.
- **Several claims are unsupported:**
  - 'A 3-port net can only do (a,b) → (a,a+b) as a loan followed by a merge.' Another design shows a single 4-port carrier, and no argument excludes other 3-port decompositions.
  - Dropping P assumes demand reaches every loaded application, which the abstract net cannot check.
- **It gives up the reversibility criterion outright.** Only pending operations can be undone.

best_ideas_to_graft: From Footprint nets: the meet/part + emit/absorb laws, where a footprint's kind is (rule, which products are out). That gives bijectivity by construction, a binary undo along one back wire, and an executable reversal check (randtest-style random forward/backward interleavings that must land exactly on the loaded net). Use this as the acceptance test for any winner.

From Footprint nets: the carry-walker binary adder. Down (c,a,b) -> (maj, a⊕c, b⊕c), up c_i = c ⊕ (a'∧b'). It is a hand-checkable 3-bit bijection whose overflow is absorbed and which leaves nothing behind, verified on 3,000 random adds.

From Tree gas: per-rule fuel bookkeeping Δf = 2 − fresh, plus ash tagged by kind for both erasure and dead work. That makes every lossy rule injective on block + bath. Extend rules.rs validate() to check these mechanically.

From Tree gas: the actual clash fix. T1·L and Sel·L have identical Unp+Eps right sides in rules.rs today; reordering Sel's arms to ⟨⟨x,b⟩,w⟩ separates them. Any reversible design built on rules.rs needs this or an equivalent.

From Tree gas: a static check that no two rules share a right-side block state. Add the missing requirement that the dice choose the same pairing from P and from Q, and redesign demand pulses and wanted bits as a true involution (as written they are not one).
From Loan net: label each rule pinned or closing (its backward branching count) as a static audit of how much drive each step needs. Also its un-append-before-read as cheap local undo.

From Three moves: the exact classifier of erased copies versus originals as the ground truth against which any local heat estimate is checked; the habit of reading a value by dispatch instead of dropping it, to catch silent data loss in two-way code; and dagger/seq written as plain disp for two-way program pairs.

From Riders: in the bead adder, each bead is popped only when its value can be recomputed from what is present. That is a clean local argument that a pop is a bijection, and it can be reused anywhere a walker parks carries.
